question: My toilet is constantly running and wasting water. I think it's the flapper, but I've never replaced one before. How do I replace the flapper on my toilet tank?
answer: Replacing the flapper on your toilet tank is a relatively simple process that can be completed with a few basic tools. First, turn off the water supply to the toilet by locating the shut-off valve behind the toilet and turning it clockwise. Next, flush the toilet to drain the tank. Then, use a wrench to loosen the nut holding the old flapper in place. Carefully lift the flapper out of the tank and dispose of it. Take the new flapper and insert the rubber valve into the hole in the tank. Align the hole in the flapper with the valve and press the flapper into place. Tighten the nut to secure the flapper. Turn the water supply back on and test the flapper by flushing the toilet several times. If the flapper is not sealing properly, you may need to adjust the nut or replace the flapper again.
